text: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise takes the caller identity from the session, the area CASE_RECORD, the right R, the case ID, the object asked about (the timer read on /cases/{caseId}/timers or the case read on /cases/{caseId}), the case attributes the scope test needs (queue, team and owner) and, for the grant, the timer type SERVICE_LEVEL or PRESCRIPTION, its status, its escalationLevel, escalatedToRole and escalatedAt; it answers with the decision code (AC-READ or AC-DENY), the matrix version used, the scope or the reason ESCALATED_TO_ROLE and the identifiers asked about.
why: Architecture v5 names the authorise operation and the TSD appendix does not publish its request or answer schema, so the attribute set has to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving it empty would stop the story and every timer read with it.
read: Arch v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 T3.1, T6.2 and T-A.1; FSD P4 A2.4, A2.7 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E1-028 sections 5 and 12

confirm: Security administrator role and the rwb-access tech lead when RWB-P4-E1037-CON is published
impact: A different attribute set changes the controller, the contract fake and every caller's client only; the decision codes, the refusal messages and the record shape stay as specified.

text: The matrix version in force at the 30 November 2026 release date is PM-2026.12, the label the FSD load examples use and the version the tests of this story name; the answer always names the version it actually read from permission.matrix_version, so a different label in force changes the answer's text and no rule.
why: No source names the matrix version in force on the release date, and the story must not copy a version label as if a source had fixed it; the FSD examples and the load path both use PM-2026.12, which is the acting default.

impact: A different version label changes the test fixture and the version named in an answer, and no rule, message or record shape.

text: When the caller's own or team scope and an escalation grant both admit the case, the answer names the scope of the escalation grant and records the reason ESCALATED_TO_ROLE, and it never reports a scope wider than the caller's role row carries; one answer is returned, one AC-READ entry is written, and the case and the timer do not move.
why: The legacy key says the breach is escalated to the named role and the case does not move, but no source says which of two admitting scopes the answer names; the story needs one answer per request and must not invent a wider scope than the policy holds.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-028 AC2 and BR3; FSD P4 A2.14; TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE; Architecture v5 slide 43

confirm: Security administrator role and the business lead role for the service level when the policy pack is approved
impact: A different ruling changes the scope named in an escalated answer and the wording of its reason, and no grant, refusal, record or switch behaviour.

text: An authorise request for the allocation key carries the capability area, the right and the business date, and then either the team code for a summary read or the case ID with its team and owner reference for a case read; the run and rerun requests carry the area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION, the right U, the job reference JOB-03 and the business date. No attribute of a case, a queue or an allocation is read from a table.
why: The request shape is the contract of RWB-P3-E1020-CON and no source fixes its attribute set for an allocation, queue or summary read, while the answer must still be built from identifiers only because the case, queue and assignment tables are P3's (DP-01, DP-11).

confirm: Security administrator role and the solution architect of rwb-access
impact: If the published request carries fewer or other attributes, the scope and case answers follow what the contract sends and the tests are rewritten against the fake; no table read is added either way.

text: The authorise request for the read-only case record carries the case reference, the owner, the queue, the team, the region, the action the caller is about to take and the field IDs the screen will show, and nothing else enters the service.
why: No source fixes the attribute set of an authorise request for the CASE_RECORD area: the legacy flow reads the case facts inside the module and the target moves them into a one-hop request under DP-11 and DP-01, so the shape has to be chosen.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-023 section 4 steps 2 to 7 and section 10; FSD P4 A2.11 and A2.14; TSD P4 T3.1 (role, permission, masking_rule); Architecture v5 slide 14 (POST /authorise takes role, scope and DoA)
impact: If the request carries a different attribute set, the scope rule compares different attributes and the contract with RWB-P3-E1023-CON changes; no policy row changes and no schema changes.

text: The authorise request for one review object carries the area DOCUMENTS, the right R or U, the item reference or the document reference, the item's review reason, its predicted type, its candidates and its candidate cases, the review team of an unattached item, which is the value of the rwb-document parameter REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED carried in the request and not read from a table, and, for a stored document, the case with its team, region and owner; the answer carries the decision, the scope it used, the matrix and masking version labels and one masked or clear marker per field ID the request named, and never a value, an extracted value or OCR text. The two rights are letters of one DOCUMENTS permission row, so R without U is the legacy access case of a team manager who may read and may not resolve.
why: No source gives the request or answer schema of POST /authorise: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives the operation with the words role, scope and DoA and no fields, TSD P4 appendix T-A does not define the path at all, and the legacy story gives the authorization column as Documents right R or U without a request shape. Without a fixed shape the four answers cannot be built, tested against the P5 fake or reviewed, and choosing business values instead would be worse than fixing an assumption.

text: The permission matrix version in force at the release date is PM-2026.12 and the masking version in force is MASK-SIT-01, the earlier state of the matrix being PM-2026.11; the answer names both labels with the business date it used, and a newly approved version reaches the answer on the next call through rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 with no deployment and no restart. The version in force is the latest valid_from on or before the business date, and no version is ever edited in place.
why: No source dates PM-2026.12 or MASK-SIT-01 or says which is in force on 30 November 2026, and FSD P4 A2.5 names MASK-SIT-01 only inside a test case; a story that names no version cannot prove the measure that a policy change needs no code release, and writing the label in code would put a business value in code.

text: The authorise request for a transfer or a hold carries the caller identity from the session, the capability area (QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION or CASE_RECORD), the right (U), the case reference, the action (transfer the case, place a legal hold, lift a legal hold), the case attributes the scope test needs (team and owner) and legalHold; a transfer request also carries the transfer reason code it will send, and the answer returns the decision, the scope used, the matrix version in force, the letters held in the area, the reason list version and the membership of the presented reason code.
why: Architecture v5 names the authorise operation and legalHold is a fact of a hold, while no source gives the request or answer shape; leaving either empty would stop the build, the contract fake and every caller client.

text: masking_rule covers the review-field IDs by row and by masking version, and this story writes no roster of its own: every field ID a request names is marked from masking_rule for the roles the caller holds and the masking version in force, and a field ID with no covering row is masked with the default marker XXXX-XX-XX. DF-DOC-015 field_value, DF-DOC-017 confirmed_by, DF-DOC-034 extracted_value, DF-DOC-080 review_reason and DF-DOC-081 review_outcome are named as identifiers of the document hub only and are never read by a statement of this story.
why: No source lists the field IDs of a review item or of a document whose fields are in REVIEW, so a roster in code would invent business values and a roster in this service's schema would duplicate the document hub's model; the ownership of document_field, document_intake and document_text is P5's, so the roster can only live with the masking rows loaded by the policy pack.
